12: A livestock or beast that the majority of its skull is fractured, either majority of height or majority laterally, is Treifah, even if its membrane is intact.

If it's reduced, and missing the area of a  sela, it's Treifah.

Rema: But less than this, it's better to declare it kosher, even nowadays when we're not worried about a perforated brain membrane (so seems to say the Tur and בא"ו הארוך כלל נ"ד)

But with waterfowl such as geese and ducks (Rashba and teshuvat haRosh 20:9), even if the skull is perforated any amount, it's Treifah.

A land bird that was bit by a weasel on its head, or was struck on wood or stone: he puts his finger on the side of the hole and presses his finger there, or puts his hand in its mouth and presses there; if the brain doesn't ooze out, it's certain the membrane of the brain isn't punctured and it's kosher.  If it comes out it's treif.

Rema: But we are not expert in checking the Treifot, consequently it's better to declare Treif if the skull is punctured any mount in a bird, even a land bird.  (בשערים דמהרא"י שער ל"א ובא"ו הארוך כלל צ"ד)
